Appreciate a quick run-through from your legal/ops — happy to do a short sync if helpful.

Best,

Thanks — I reviewed Helio_MSA_Redlines_v3.docx and captured suggested clean language for rollback protection below (aiming for narrow operational commitment):

"Rollback Protection: Vendor shall provide rollback support for deployments that introduce a material change to the API behavior impacting Customer production traffic. Vendor will coordinate rollback actions with Customer within thirty (30) calendar days of written request by Customer’s authorized contacts. Rollback activities are limited to reversing deployment artifacts and restoring the most recent known-good model/configuration. Vendor will maintain an on-call escalation contact for rollback coordination during business hours; emergency support outside of business hours may be subject to separate support arrangements."

Notes:
- Suggest we define "material change" by reference to a short list (model architecture switch, schema change to responses, or changes to tokenization/config that alter outputs).
- This language is intended as an operational commitment, not a warranty of output parity; so it should not trigger indemnity or SLA changes.

On SOW traceability: we prefer a one-page mapping table in Exhibit B (SOW) that pairs: milestone ID | deliverable | Order Form SKU | invoicing trigger. Jonas: can you produce the initial mapping in the attached SOW_change_map.xlsx and flag any deliverables that might be considered new scope?

If no new deliverables, this should be a clean contract update (no price impact). If the implementation team needs additional acceptance testing hours or extended rollback windows beyond 30 days, that could create a fee note — we should be explicit.

I’m available for the 9:30 PT sync. 

Laura Bennett
